items.title: The potentially deadly substance being delivered to Aussie doors at all hours
items.description: The importation of nitrous oxide has exploded in the last decade. Nangs are increasingly being used by some to chase a high and causing significant damage.

items.title: Hanson's Socceroos own goal should have been a free kick for Taylor
items.description: Pauline Hanson has chosen one of Australia's most popular national sporting brands and visible expressions of cultural diversity in her pitch for a "monoculture".

items.title: As Europeans swelter, can they learn from Australians?
items.description: Europe's record-breaking heatwave has highlighted its vulnerability to climate change. But countries could look to Australia's experience with scorching summers to learn valuable lessons.

items.title: Karl Stefanovic to reportedly leave Channel Nine after Tommy Robinson podcast
items.description: Today show host Karl Stefanovic is set to leave Channel Nine after a podcast interview with British far-right figure Tommy Robinson, Nine Newspapers is reporting.

items.title: ASIO warns of 'unprecedented threats' and defends pre-Bondi resourcing
items.description: Australia's domestic spy chief, Mike Burgess, has defended the agency's resourcing decisions in the years leading up to the Bondi terror attack, arguing his agency is grappling with an "unprecedented" volume of threats.

items.title: Live: Jam-packed day as last round of World Cup group clashes kicks off
items.description: The final round of the group stage at the 2026 FIFA World Cup starts with simultaneous Group B games between Switzerland and Canada, and Qatar vs Bosnia and Herzegovina. Follow live.

items.title: How a discarded coffee cup helped solve a 24-year cold case killing
items.description: Twenty-four years after the killing of a Canberra grandmother, a coffee cup discarded on an east coast road trip leads to the arrest and convictions of her killers.

items.title: Sydney, Melbourne tipped to lead housing price drops as market cools
items.description: House price falls of up to 7 and 8 per cent in Sydney and Melbourne have been forecast for the year ahead, according to Domain. But it's far from doom and gloom for existing owners, with resale profits hitting a record.

items.title: These volcanic islands are uninhabited, but two nations are fighting over them
items.description: Tensions are rising between Vanuatu and France as they negotiate a sovereignty dispute over two volcanic islands, believed to be inhabited by a god.

items.title: Knights player Kepaoa banned for six weeks for homophobic slur
items.description: Newcastle Knights player Asu Kepaoa is handed a six-week ban for using a homophobic slur during a NSW Cup match.

items.title: Small designers hitting roadblocks trying to get support against Shein copies
items.description: Small Australian fashion designers who have had their designs copied by overseas ultra-fast fashion companies say they have hit continuous roadblocks trying to get support.

items.title: The passion, pride and chaos of World Cup fan culture
items.description: Every four years, the World Cup provides the perfect backdrop for fans to showcase their culture's traditional football rituals in front of millions.

items.title: Deadly bird flu discovered in second Australian state
items.description: A third confirmed case of the deadly H5 bird flu has been found in a migratory bird on Australia's southern coast.

items.title: Police to review case of Epstein accuser Virginia Giuffre
items.description: The interactions Jeffery Epstein accuser Virginia Giuffre had with Australian police before her death will be reviewed, WA's police commissioner confirms.

items.title: What happened when I embraced the Swedish right to camp anywhere you want
items.description: I've hated camping since I was a teenager, but embracing the spirit of Sweden's Allemansrätten — the right to camp wherever you like — changed everything.

items.title: Put your Australian film knowledge to the test
items.description: Think you know your Mad Max from your Muriel's Wedding? Take our Australian film quiz to find out.

items.title: Anna saw gambling as harmless fun. Here's what she wished she knew
items.description: Experts say the gambling industry is increasingly targeting women, and there are potential risks with a novelty bet.

items.title: Neil the seal is back bigger than ever — and that's a problem
items.description: Neil, an elephant seal well known to Tasmanians, has returned to land and a video shows him being coerced off a road for his own safety.

items.title: France reports first Ebola case in doctor returning from DRC
items.description: France has confirmed its first case of Ebola, a doctor who had flown back from the Democratic Republic of Congo.

items.title: Award-winning artist accused of copying second artwork
items.description: Australian artist Jane Allan, revealed to have previously copied another painter's work, is being accused of a second case of imitation.

items.title: Bird flu has arrived in Australia
items.description: After years of waiting, the deadly H5N1 strain of bird flu has finally arrived in Australia. Two birds found on the southern coast of Western Australia near Esperance have been confirmed as infected, but there is no evidence so far of a mass-mortality event. So, what actually is H5N1, and why does it matter?

items.title: Has One Nation won the 'family feud' of Australian conservatives?
items.description: There's a "family feud" in Australia's political right, and right now it appears One Nation is winning.

items.title: Gina Rinehart names veterans' accommodation after Ben Roberts-Smith
items.description: Australia's richest person has opened a facility for homeless veterans in a beachside Perth suburb.

items.title: Will Congress demanding US military halt action in Iran end the war?
items.description: The US Senate approved a war powers resolution seeking to block military action against Iran on Tuesday. But don't expect the war to end.

items.title: Showers to chase away the chill of Queensland's winter
items.description: A warm change will arrive in Queensland this weekend, along with scattered rain and warnings of strong winds in the north.
